title: Staged Release Conductor for Variant Attenuation and Auto-rollback
creator: Marco Liu
description: Goal: Build a 'Release Conductor' policy engine that orchestrates staged model variant introductions with fine-grained traffic attenuation, shadow probing, A/B allocations, and automatic rollback when guardrails are violated. This is a runtime+control-plane feature: the control plane compiles rollout policies into executable plans, and the runtime enforces traffic splits and probes while streaming telemetry back to the conductor. The engine must support: (1) deterministic step schedules (time or event-driven), (2) adaptive steps that pause on signal degradation, (3) shadow traffic probes for quality regressions, (4) A/B allocations with metrics correlation, and (5) auto-rollback thresholds with configurable dampening (e.g., require N consecutive windows). This ticket covers the first MVP: the rollout DSL grammar, policy compiler, enforcement hooks, telemetry schema, and a staged rollout simulator for validation and canary playground tests.
acceptance_criteria: DSL defined and documented (examples for time-based, event-based, and adaptive steps)
Policy compiler produces plan JSON that the runtime 'variant-router' understands
Runtime enforces traffic splits for both live and shadow traffic without adding >1ms median p50 latency per request in staging
Guardrails implemented: HTTP error rate, p99 latency, and quality regression (embedding similarity delta) trigger pause/rollback
Auto-rollback executes a safe revert: immediate traffic cutover to previous stable variant and a rollback event recorded in audit logs
E2E tests simulate a 5-step rollout with injected regression and verify rollback behavior
Design doc and README with migration notes for existing canary configs
implementation_notes: Control plane: rollout DSL -> policy compiler -> plan (immutable) stored in rollout-store (etcd)
Runtime adapter: variant-router accepts plan version + delta; supports 'apply', 'pause', 'rollback' commands over control-channel
Telemetry: use unified rollout telemetry stream (rollout_id, step, traffic_split, metrics_snapshot) emitted to metrics-store for alerts and to timeline API for console visualization
Guardrail evaluation: sliding window (configurable window_size, step_granularity). Must support composite rules (AND/OR) and tie-breakers (severity-weighted)
Shadow traffic: routed to candidate variant with sampled request context; responses logged and compared offline using evaluation harness
Rollback policy: require either (a) immediate critical alarm OR (b) 3 out of 5 consecutive windows exceeding thresholds; operator override allowed
Backward compatibility: existing 'canary' entries to be converted to DSL via migration script; runtime will accept legacy 'simple-split' payloads for 3 months
sample_dsl:
wave:
  id: wave-2025-02-18-01
  variants:
    - id: vstable
      weight: 100
    - id: v2-quant
      weight: 0
  steps:
    - name: init-shadow
      duration: 10m
      action: shadow
      shadow_percentage: 5
    - name: staged-shift
      duration: 30m
      action: ramp
      target_weights: {vstable: 90, v2-quant: 10}
    - name: adaptive-step
      duration: 60m
      action: adaptive-ramp
      target_weights: {vstable: 70, v2-quant: 30}
      guardrails:
        - metric: error_rate_5xx
          op: less_than
          threshold: 0.005
        - metric: quality_delta_embedding_mean
          op: less_than
          threshold: 0.02
      pause_on_trigger: true
  rollback_policy:
    immediate_on: ["error_rate_5xx>0.02"]
    windowed_on: {windows: 5, failures_required: 3, signal: "quality_delta_embedding_p95>0.05"}
testing_plan: Unit tests for policy compiler grammar and plan validation (parser fuzzing)
Staging e2e: deploy conductor + runtime image to staging cluster; run 5-step rollout with failure injection that increases error_rate and embedding delta; assert rollback occurs
Chaos test: kill candidate variant pods mid-step to ensure step resumption and safe attenuation happens
Integration: console visualization of rollout timeline and a 'manual abort' button wired to control-plane API
Performance: measure p50/p95 added latency on routing path under 1ms/5ms respectively with 95% CI
Security: ensure audit log includes rollout plan hash, user, and timestamps for all apply/rollback actions
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: noisy quality metric causing flapping -> Mitigation: require consecutive-window gating + severity weighting
Risk: undercounting shadow traffic due to sampling -> Mitigation: deterministic sampling seed for reproducibility and increase sample for evaluation windows
Risk: operator confusion with automated rollbacks -> Mitigation: explicit human-in-the-loop modes and console warnings; opt-out flag for fully-automated rollbacks
Risk: performance regression from routing layer -> Mitigation: benchmark harness and runtime perf budget (p50<1ms added)
Risk: config explosion from DSL -> Mitigation: provide safe presets and a 'simple' mode that compiles to conservative defaults
migration_notes: Provide a migration script control-plane/migrations/2025-02-rc-migrate.sh that converts legacy canary entries into 'wave' DSL with conservative defaults
Decommission plan: deprecate legacy simple-canary API after two release cycles and convert customers with >7 days notice
